_about: The channel's own identity. gen_image.py and thumbnail.py draw the mascot from it, the short-script skill packages every video in its style, upload.py takes its settings from it. Change the channel here, not in the scripts. The two null fields under upload are a person's decision: upload.py refuses to publish until both are true or false.
name: Querious
promise: One surprising question about the everyday world, answered with real sources by a cartoon mascot that acts it out.
audience: Curious teens and adults who like quick science, engineering, nature and history answers. English.
_angle: The twist that makes this channel different from the big channels in the same topics: a different mascot, world or audience, never a copy of another channel's look. Written by the mascot design step (cutout-cartoon-shorts skill, section 12.1) when empty.

mascot.name: engineer
mascot.look: simple white character with a big round head, a small soft body, noodle arms with simple four-finger hands and short legs with rounded feet, thick smooth black outlines of even weight, flat white fill with a very soft pale-grey shade on one side, small solid black oval eyes, simple curved black eyebrows, no nose, no hair, no clothes, a pink tongue only when the mouth is open
mascot._help: look = how every character picture is drawn (written to follow 'a' / 'the same'). signature = one ownable detail that is always visible and readable at thumbnail size (a colour, a prop, a silhouette). library = the folder in library/characters/. chosen = true once a person or the mascot design step has settled it.

packaging.thumbnail_style: The mascot big and close with one clear emotion, beside the one thing the video is about; a simple flat background in one or two bold colours that contrast with both; one focal point; readable at phone size.

upload._help: made_for_kids: true when children are the main audience (COPPA; it turns off comments and personalised ads). contains_synthetic_media: true when anything could be mistaken for real, for example a realistic AI voice of a real person; YouTube then adds a label. category_id 27 = Education, 28 = Science & Technology, 24 = Entertainment. zernio_account_id: the YouTube account's _id from `upload.py --accounts`.
